title: IQR of a short odd list
source: Theory S1-3.2 Quick check 1 (IQR 8); new even IQR from Q3-Q1
stem: An ordered data set has lower quartile {q1|int} and upper quartile {q3|int}. What is the interquartile range of this data set?

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: The interquartile range of a data set is {q3|int}-{q1|int}={A|int}.

title: Least possible interquartile range from a grouped table

source.note: 9709/61/M/J/14 Question 7(iii) only [3], with the opening table. Official QP and official MS. Parts (i) and (ii) omitted.

stem:
This question is 9709/61/M/J/14 Question 7(iii) only, taken from the official QP. The opening table is included so that the part is self-contained.

A typing test is taken by 111 people. The numbers of typing errors they make in the test are summarised in the table below.

Number of typing errors: 1-5, 6-20, 21-35, 36-60, 61-80.
Frequency: 24, 9, 21, 15, 42.

(iii) State which class contains the lower quartile and which class contains the upper quartile. Hence find the least possible value of the interquartile range. [3]

steps.name: L
steps.text_tex: The lower quartile is in the class 6–20.
steps.note: Official MS: B1, LQ in 6-20. Cumulative frequencies 24, 33, 54, 69, 111. The 28th value (about n/4) is in 6-20.

steps.name: U
steps.text_tex: The upper quartile is in the class 61–80.
steps.note: Official MS: B1, UQ in 61-80. The 84th value (about 3n/4) is in 61-80.

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: The least possible value of the interquartile range is \(61-20=41\).
steps.note: Official MS: B1, 61-20=41, follow through any or both wrong quartile classes if sensible. Independent: the largest possible Q1 in 6-20 is 20 and the smallest possible Q3 in 61-80 is 61.

contexts.note: Stem taken from the official QP PDF (UCLES 2014), Question 7(iii) only, with the opening table. Official MS reproduced mark by mark. Paper/self-mark.
